title: A Criterion for Covariance in Complex Sequential Growth Models
version: arXiv:2003.11311v1 (25 Mar 2020; only version listed). Published version doi 10.1088/1361-6382/ab987f (Class. Quantum Grav. 2020) identified via Crossref; publisher text not compared with v1.
section_locator: Sec. 1; Sec. 2 (cylinder sets Eqs. (1)-(3), covariant set Eq. (4), proof that no nontrivial event in the finite-stage algebra is covariant, originary event Eq. (5)); Sec. 2.1 (conditions (a)-(c), footnote 4, Eqs. (6)-(10)); Sec. 2.2 (Eqs. (11)-(16)); Sec. 2.3 (variation Eq. (17), Theorem 2.1, Eq. (19)); Sec. 3.1 (Theorem 3.1, Claims 3.2-3.3); Sec. 3.2 (Lemmas 3.4-3.5, Eq. (45), Corollary 3.6); Sec. 3.3 (Corollary 3.7, Claims 3.8-3.9, Eqs. (47)-(62)); Sec. 4 (Eqs. (63)-(67)); Appendices A-B.
relevance: Primary statement of when a complex (C-valued) sequential-growth quantum measure extends from the finite-stage labelled event algebra to its sigma-algebra and hence to covariant events. Decisive for RC-4 quantum region: where extension fails, only label-dependent finite-stage events carry a measure.
assumptions: C-valued vector measure (histories Hilbert space ~ C) built multiplicatively from transition amplitudes along the unique labelled path (Eq. (16)); internal temporality; covariance imposed as equality of amplitudes of order-isomorphic labelled nodes (condition (a), Sec. 2.2); Markov sum rule for amplitudes (Eq. (14)); spectator independence in the C case giving the Rideout-Sorkin form with complex t_n (Eq. (15)); Theorem 2.1 derived from the Caratheodory-Hahn-Kluvanek theorem for H ~ C (App. B).
conclusion: Theorem 2.1: the complex measure on the finite-stage algebra has a unique extension to the generated sigma-algebra iff it is of bounded variation. Theorem 3.1/Corollary 3.6: bounded variation if sum of zeta_n^a converges; not of bounded variation if sum of zeta_n^c diverges (antichain and chain nodes give the max and min, Lemmas 3.4-3.5). Corollary 3.7: all t_k in R+ extends. Claim 3.8: finitely many couplings extend if m=1 and k_1>1, or k_m-k_{m-1}>1; do not extend if only t_1 is nonzero and not in R+. Claim 3.9: a countable family with asymptotically collinear couplings extends. Complex percolation extends only for q in [0,1] (Eqs. (60)-(62), reproving [15]). Sec. 2: no event in the finite-stage algebra is covariant except Omega. Authors do not claim that birth order becomes physical in non-extending models; they call extending models 'consistent covariant dynamics'.
proof_status: Hand proofs in paper; Claims 3.8-3.9 rely on large-n dominant-term asymptotics (Eqs. (48)-(57)); the case k_m-k_{m-1}=1 with m>1 is explicitly left undecided ('this is not sufficient to prove divergence'). Not reproduced here.
dependencies: Rudin Theorem 6.4 (complex measures on sigma-algebras have bounded variation)
open_questions: Bounded variation when k_m - k_{m-1} = 1 for m > 1 (Sec. 3.3.1, left open by authors).
Measures of covariant events other than the originary event in extending models (Sec. 4, deferred).

Whether conditional-convergence prescriptions (Sorkin MSCS 2012, cited as [17]) give covariant measures for non-extending models such as complex percolation; Sorkin-Surya 'in preparation' [18] not read.
limits: Read from arXiv HTML render of v1 (LaTeXML); math transcribed from alttext. No PDF page numbers used. Earlier KB record for this ID was discovery depth; this record upgrades it and should become canonical after coordinator review. Physical interpretation of quantum measures (preclusion, co-events) taken from authors' text only.

title: Observables in causal set cosmology
version: arXiv:gr-qc/0210061v2 (20 Oct 2002); Phys. Rev. D 67, 084031 (2003), doi 10.1103/PhysRevD.67.084031 (from arXiv page; publisher text not compared). arXiv title carries quotation marks around 'Observables'.
section_locator: Abstract; Sec. 1; Sec. 2 (generalized percolation Eq. (1), 'is element 3 above element 1?' passage, definition of covariant sigma-algebra R); Sec. 3 (stem sets, Theorem 1, Propositions 1-2, Corollary 1, Gamma counterexample, rogues); Sec. 4 (Lemmas 1-4, Corollaries 2-3); Sec. 5 (Theorem 2, Mackey); Sec. 6 (Lemmas 6-9, mu = mu~|R = mu~ o p^-1); Sec. 7 (discussion, open questions).
relevance: Defines covariant observables in CSG as label-invariant measurable sets and proves stem sets generate them up to measure zero; states that the labelled process answers label-dependent questions that are 'not meaningful'. Confirms the defeat-search note's quotes.
assumptions: Generic CSG (generalized percolation) with real t_k >= 0 and t_k > 0 for some k >= 2 (Sec. 2); dust and forest cases handled separately as deterministic (Sec. 7); all relabelings treated as pure gauge.
conclusion: Corollary 1: for every covariant measurable A there is B in the stem-generated sigma-algebra with mu(A sym-diff B) = 0, in any CSG dynamics. mu on unlabelled completed causets is the restriction/pushforward of the labelled measure (Sec. 6). Authors leave open whether a label-free dynamics would give a different physical measure and whether all relabelings are gauge (Sec. 7).
proof_status: Full proofs given (Lemmas 1-9); Prop. 2 uses Mackey's theorem on Borel subquotients of Polish spaces. Not independently re-derived.
dependencies: Mackey 1976 (countable separating family generates in Borel subquotient of Polish space)
open_questions: Would a fundamentally label-free dynamics give a different physical measure? (Sec. 7, 'We do not know.')
Should all relabelings be pure gauge or only finite-support ones? (Sec. 7)
Non-generic CSG models outside generalized percolation (conjecture, Sec. 7).
limits: Read from arXiv HTML of v2; no page numbers. The defeat-search note's page locators (p.4-5, p.16-17) could not be checked against PDF pagination; section locators substituted. No observer or record model in the paper.

title: General Covariance and the "Problem of Time" in a Discrete Cosmology
version: arXiv:gr-qc/0202097v1 (27 Feb 2002), SU-GP-2001/12-1; ANPA 23 proceedings (Correlations, ed. K. Bowden, 2002, pp. 1-17 per later citations). No DOI found.
section_locator: Abstract; Sec. 1; Sec. 3 (stochastic process construction); Sec. 4 'Two meanings of general covariance'; Sec. 5 'What are the covariant questions?' (3-chain example, footnote distinguishing unanswerable from meaningless); Sec. 6 (stem sets, Conjecture, proof sketch (a)-(c)); Sec. 7 (conclusion: determinism remark, quantum hurdles, 'this particular stem' conditional-probability question).
relevance: The named problem-of-time/birth-order paper. States the two roles of discrete general covariance, that stage-indexed questions ('Do the first three elements form a 3-chain?') are not covariant, and raises the only indexical/self-locating question found in this literature ('this particular copy of S1 ... that we inhabit').
assumptions: Generic classical CSG; covariance as relabeling invariance; cosmological (whole-causet) probabilities only.
conclusion: Authors: covariant questions are exactly label-invariant measurable sets; stem predicates give them physical meaning (conjecture, later proved in gr-qc/0210061). Quantum case faces two hurdles: interpretation of the quantum measure and unboundedness of complex amplitudes breaking the extension theorems. Open: whether a logically independent conditional probability for 'this particular stem' is needed, which 'would re-open the problem of time in a new context'.
proof_status: Talk write-up; conjecture with a three-step proof sketch (a)-(c) attributed to work in preparation; the full proof is in gr-qc/0210061.
dependencies: Dynkin, Markov Processes (construction of the measure)
open_questions: Is an independent notion of conditional probability needed for questions about 'this particular' stem 'that we inhabit' (Sec. 7)? Unanswered by authors.
Quantum analogue of the stem conjecture (Sec. 7).
limits: Conference talk text. Read from arXiv HTML of v1. Contains no formal observer or record model; the 'we inhabit' passage is a question, not a construction.

title: Observables in Extended Percolation Models of Causal Set Cosmology
version: arXiv:gr-qc/0504069v1 (15 Apr 2005); Class. Quantum Grav. 23 (2006) 1381-1390, doi 10.1088/0264-9381/23/4/018 (from arXiv page; publisher text not compared).
section_locator: Sec. 1 (GP, WBC, EP definitions, Eqs. (1)-(4)); Sec. 2 (eras, turtles/yertles, Claim 1 on breaks); Sec. 3 (Proposition 1, Lemma 1, Corollary 1, Proposition 2, Claim 2); Sec. 4.1 (why Bell causality involves ratios; VSBC); Sec. 4.2 (PBC weaker than WBC); Appendix (PBC + GC => EP).
relevance: Extended percolation is the general solution of Markov sum rule + general covariance + weak Bell causality (per Rideout-Varadarajan); era couplings depend on the realised earlier causet, yet the dynamics stays covariant. Stem-set completeness extends to EP. Shows history dependence is not the same as path dependence.
assumptions: Markovian; general covariance (label independence); WBC or PBC; transition probabilities may vanish.
conclusion: Proposition 1/2: in any EP the stem sets generate the covariant sigma-algebra up to measure zero. Sec. 4.1: Bell causality is imposed 'at the level of the labelled (non-covariant) process'; whether its implications for the covariant measure can be understood in stem terms is open. Sec. 4.2: WBC alone forces GC on certain path pairs.
proof_status: Proofs given in paper and appendix; relies on Brightwell et al. rogue characterization. Not re-derived.
open_questions: Can the implications of Bell causality for the covariant measure be expressed in stem predicates? (Sec. 4.1, authors)
Is BC the unique physical causality condition? (Sec. 4.1, 'remains unsettled')
limits: Read from arXiv HTML of v1. Classical only. Era-dependence on earlier causets is covariant (depends on unlabelled stacks), so it is not an order-dependent dynamics in the RC-4 sense.

title: On extending the Quantum Measure
version: arXiv:1007.2725v1 (16 Jul 2010); J. Phys. A 43 (2010) 505305, doi 10.1088/1751-8113/43/50/505305 (from arXiv page; publisher text not compared).
section_locator: Sec. 1 (quantum sum rule Eq. (1), no known Caratheodory-Kolmogorov analogue); Sec. 2 opening (decoherence functional axioms); Sec. 4 (complex percolation, product decoherence functional Eqs. (42)-(43), p+q=1, Lemma 1, Claims 4-5, Eqs. (46)-(58)); Sec. 5 (discussion: labelled events not observables, conditional convergence by preferred ordering, complexified Euler function Eq. (59), Claims 6-7).
relevance: First proof that complex percolation's quantum vector measure does not extend unless p is real in [0,1]; states that in the causal-set case finite-stage (labelled) events are not observables, so non-extension removes covariant observables; proposes conditional convergence keyed to a preferred ordering of events as a remedy.
assumptions: Strongly positive decoherence functional; product form D = A* A for complex percolation (histories Hilbert space ~ C); transitive-percolation transition structure with complex p, q.
conclusion: Lemma 1: complex percolation vector measure is not of bounded variation for non-real p (Claims 4-5 cover |p|>1 or |q|>1). Real p in [0,1] extends; then all classical covariant observables of transitive percolation are observables of real quantum percolation and stem sets generate them up to measure zero (Sec. 5). Claim 7: a two-state unitary example where every finite-time event except Omega lies in a set of quantum measure zero.
proof_status: Hand proofs in paper; Sec. 3 (finite unitary systems) not read in detail.
open_questions: Is there a unique preferred ordering for conditional convergence, and does it give covariant predictions? (Sec. 5, authors: 'important to ensure that such an ordering procedure is unique')
Does a complexification of classical covariant probabilities define a genuine bi-additive quantum measure? (Sec. 5)
limits: Read Secs. 1, 2 (opening), 4 and 5 in full from arXiv HTML; Sec. 3 not read in detail. No observer or record model.

title: Implementing Bell causality in Quantum Sequential Growth
version: arXiv:2603.25503v1 (26 Mar 2026); preprint, no DOI found.
section_locator: Abstract; Sec. 1; Sec. 2.2 (generalised measure Def., Eqs. (8)-(16), MSR/GC/BC items 1-3); Sec. 3 (decoherence functional and vector measure definitions, Eqs. (23)-(30)); Sec. 3.1 (QSG dynamics, Eqs. (31)-(33), General Covariance paragraph and 'Note' on phases); Sec. 3.2 opening (Eqs. (34)-(37), Lemma 3.1); Sec. 4 Discussion (Eq. (149), path-dependent phase remark).
relevance: Most recent primary work on operator-valued (non-commutative) quantum sequential growth. Imposes GC as equality of labelled-path vectors and explicitly sets aside a weaker norm-only (phase) covariance in which labelled paths would carry path-dependent phases - the place where label information could enter interference.
assumptions: Finitely additive vector measure on the labelled cylinder algebra; transition operators composed in strict stage order (Eq. (31)); GC as |c_n> = |c_n'> for order-isomorphic nodes; non-singular transition operators; three operator orderings for quantum Bell causality (TOBC, NTOBC, CPOBC).
conclusion: Authors' results (abstract and Sec. 1): for the two most natural QBC orderings the transition-operator algebra becomes commutative (back to C-valued models); CPOBC gives new commutation relations without commutativity; a d=2 Pauli representation is inconsistent. GC as stated has 'no operator ordering ambiguity, since A_gamma is strictly time ordered' (Sec. 3.1). Norm-only covariance with path-dependent phases is noted but not pursued (Sec. 3.1 Note; Sec. 4).
proof_status: Lemmas/Theorem 3.7 and appendix calculations not read; results taken as authors' claims. Recent preprint, not peer reviewed as far as checked.
open_questions: Covariance only of the norm, with path-dependent phases (Sec. 3.1 Note; Sec. 4): dynamics 'becomes rapidly more complex'; not analysed.
Existence of a non-trivial non-commutative representation; extension of such a measure to the sigma-algebra (Sec. 4).
limits: Read Secs. 1, 2.2, 3, 3.1, 3.2 (opening) and 4 from arXiv HTML; Secs. 2.1, 2.3-2.4, 3.3-3.5 and Appendix not read. No observer or record model.

title: A manifestly covariant framework for causal set dynamics
version: arXiv:1910.07292v2 (25 Mar 2020); Class. Quantum Grav. 37 (2020) 085003, doi 10.1088/1361-6382/ab719c (from arXiv page; publisher text not compared).
section_locator: Sec. 1 (two facets of covariance; footnote 3 on DGC); Sec. 2.3 (cylinder sets as stage events, covariant sub-sigma-algebra); Sec. 2.4 (DGC, BC Eq. (2), Eq. (3)-(5)); Sec. 3 (covtree motivation); Sec. 4 (Lemma 4.1, Theorem 4.2); Sec. 4.1 (Lemmas 4.8-4.9); Sec. 5 (questions (i)-(v)).
relevance: Lemma 4.9 and Sec. 5: every walk on labelled poscau, 'whether it satisfies Discrete General Covariance or not', has a covtree walk producing the same measure on the stem algebra. Directly bounds what any non-path-independent labelled dynamics can show in covariant (stem) events.
assumptions: Classical probability measures; stem algebra R(S) as physical observables; Lusin-space extension theorem for Lemma 4.9.
conclusion: Lemma 4.8: R(S) equals the sigma-algebra generated by covtree certificate sets. Lemma 4.9: every measure on R(S) extends to the labelled sigma-algebra. Hence covtree measures = poscau measures on R(S); no easy relation between DGC and manifest covariance (Sec. 5).
proof_status: Proofs given (Lemma 4.9 cites a measure-extension theorem for Lusin spaces). Not re-derived.
open_questions: Covtree condition equivalent to DGC only, i.e. order-invariance (Sec. 5 (i))
Covtree condition equivalent to CSG (Sec. 5 (ii))
Covariant causality condition (Sec. 5 (iii))
Quantum walk on covtree (Sec. 5 (v))
limits: Read Secs. 1-2, 3 (opening), 4 (statements; Lemmas 4.3-4.7 proofs skimmed), 4.1 and 5 from arXiv HTML. Classical only.

title: Order-invariant measures on causal sets
version: arXiv:0901.0240v3 (21 Sep 2011); Ann. Appl. Probab. (2011), doi 10.1214/10-AAP736 (DOI from arXiv/Crossref; publisher text not compared).
section_locator: Abstract; Sec. 1 (Examples 1-3; interpretation of Rideout-Sorkin general covariance as order-invariance); Sec. 4 (definition Eq. (4), order-Markov, Eq. (5), Lemma 4.1, Theorem 4.2); Sec. 5 (fixed-causet processes, Example 4: two chains, mu_q and Polya urn; independent-label processes incl. random graph orders); Sec. 6 (Lemma 6.1, Theorems 6.2-6.3); Sec. 7 (Theorems 7.1-7.2, Corollary 7.6, Conjecture 7.7, Theorem 7.8); Sec. 8 (Theorem 8.1 statement and discussion).
relevance: Prior published statement of the RC-4(a) property: conditional on the stage-k causal set, every order of generation is equally likely, and this is how the authors read Rideout-Sorkin general covariance. Also shows non-uniqueness of order-invariant measures on a fixed infinite causal set (Example 4), the missing completed-infinite case of the coordinator's note.
assumptions: Causet processes on Omega = pairs (label string in [0,1]^N, suborder of N); probability measures; order-invariance Eq. (4).
conclusion: Theorem 4.2: mu is order-invariant iff mu(E) = E_mu nu^k(E) for every E and k, where nu^k is uniform over linear extensions of the first-k poset (a DLR-type characterization). Theorem 7.2: extremal iff trivial tails. Corollary 7.6: unique decomposition into extremal order-invariant measures. Theorem 8.1: structure of extremal measures. Example 4: on two disjoint infinite chains every q in [0,1] gives an order-invariant mu_q.
proof_status: Full proofs in paper (Secs. 7-8 use backward martingale convergence and Georgii/Maitra results). Sec. 8 proofs (Lemmas 8.2-8.8) not read.
dependencies: Georgii, Gibbs Measures and Phase Transitions
open_questions: Conjecture 7.7: an order-invariant measure generated by some omega is extremal.
Classification of extremal order-invariant measures on fixed causal sets (stated as likely prohibitively difficult, Sec. 1).
limits: Read Secs. 1, 4, 5, 6 (opening), 7 (statements and Example 4 discussion) and 8 (statement) from arXiv HTML. Purely mathematical: no physical interpretation of tail statistics, no observer model.

title: Order-invariant measures on fixed causal sets
version: arXiv:0901.0242v2 (29 Jan 2012); Combinatorics, Probability and Computing (2012), doi 10.1017/S0963548311000721 (Crossref; publisher text not compared).

conclusion: Authors: 'depending on P, there may be one, many, or no order-invariant probability measures'; sufficient conditions for existence and uniqueness are given in the body (not read).
proof_status: Only Sec. 1 read; main theorems not read.
open_questions: Which fixed causal sets admit a unique order-invariant measure (body of paper, not read).
limits: Introduction only read in full; the existence/uniqueness theorems are unread. Read depth is full-text for Sec. 1 only.

title: If time had no beginning: growth dynamics for past-infinite causal sets
version: arXiv:2109.10749v1 (2021); Class. Quantum Grav. (2022), doi 10.1088/1361-6382/ac445f (Crossref; publisher text not compared).
section_locator: Sec. 1 footnote on the term 'observable'; Sec. 3 opening; Sec. 3.1 (alternating growth, Definition 3.2, Lemma 3.3); Sec. 3.2 (Eqs. (3)-(8), Lemma 3.4, Claim 3.5, Covariance and Causality paragraphs, Claim 3.6 statement); Sec. 5 Discussion.
relevance: Gives explicit growth dynamics that violate discrete general covariance: every Alternating CSG model other than Alternating Transitive Percolation (Claim 3.5). Authors keep covariant convex-events as observables and note that causality conditions for non-covariant models become label-dependent.
assumptions: Alternating (past and future) sequential growth with Rideout-Sorkin couplings; DGC generalised to alternating poscau.
conclusion: Claim 3.5: an Alternating CSG model satisfies DGC iff it is Alternating Transitive Percolation. Lemma 3.4: TP and ATP agree on every finite-stage labelled probability (only for TP) yet differ when run to infinity. Authors read the results as 'evidence against the existence of physically meaningful dynamical growth models for two-way infinite causal sets' (Sec. 5).
proof_status: Claim 3.5 proved by a two-labelling counterexample (Fig. 3); other proofs not checked.
open_questions: Physical interpretation of causality in non-covariant alternating dynamics (Sec. 3.2, authors).
Whether any alternating CSG dynamics gives a rich class of convex-events (Sec. 5).
limits: Read Secs. 1 (footnote), 3-3.2 and 5; Sec. 4 (Z-covtree) not read. Classical only.

title: Relativity theory does not imply that the future already exists: a counterexample
version: arXiv:gr-qc/0703098v1 (20 Mar 2007); chapter in V. Petkov (ed.), Relativity and the Dimensionality of the World (Springer 2007), doi 10.1007/978-1-4020-6318-3_9 (from arXiv page).

title: Causal Set Quantum Gravity and the Hard Problem of Consciousness
version: arXiv:2209.07653v2 (21 May 2023); no DOI found on arXiv page.
section_locator: Abstract; Sec. 4.2 (dynamical hypothesis; three concepts (a)-(c)); Sec. 4.3 'No objective external picture of the birth process'; Sec. 4.4 'A partly subjective external picture of the process'; Sec. 4.5; Sec. 4.6 'An objective internal view'.
